items.title: Corporate Bonds vs. Dividend Stocks: Which Pays a Retiree More Reliably?
items.summary: Corporate bond yields just hit a 12-month high, yet that fat payout hides trade-offs in price risk, reinvestment, and taxes. For retirees weighing bonds against Procter & Gamble and Coca-Cola, the tax bill may decide the winner.

items.title: Warren Buffett and Greg Abel Collect Billions From These Untouchable Berkshire Hathaway Dividend Stocks
items.summary: Five Berkshire holdings never budged in the latest 13F, yet their yields range from a sliver to a hefty payout. Which ones actually deliver income for retirees, and which carry risks that could trim the checks?

items.title: MCO Embeds Connected Intelligence in AI Platforms to Support Growth
items.summary: Moody's integrates proprietary intelligence into AI platforms via zero-copy data sharing & MCP connectors, aiming to expand analytics engagement & monetization.

items.title: Are Wall Street Analysts Predicting Moody's Stock Will Climb or Sink?
items.summary: Moody’s has underperformed the broader market. However, Wall Street’s outlook suggests the stock still has room to rebound.

items.title: Resource Label Group joins default ranks after missing interest payments on leveraged loan
items.summary: S&P Global Ratings on Nov. 23 downgraded RLG Holdings, the indirect parent of Resource Label Group LLC, to D, from CCC and a negative outlook, after the agency said the company failed to pay interest on its revolver, first-lien term loan and second-lien term loan within the 10-business-day grace periods following their Oct. 30 due dates. items.title: Moody’s affirms Sanofi’s Aa3 rating, shifts outlook to negative on Insmed deal
items.summary: Investing.com -- Moody’s Ratings affirmed Sanofi's (NASDAQ:SNY) Aa3 long-term issuer and senior unsecured ratings while revising its outlook to negative from stable, signaling heightened scrutiny over the pharmaceutical giant’s balance sheet following its $41 billion agreement to acquire Insmed Incorporated. items.title: Warren Buffett’s Favorite Type of Stock Is Perfect for Patient Investors
items.summary: Buffett once held hundreds of positions, yet only a tiny few have survived a decade. Coca-Cola, American Express and Moody's earned their spots, but one of them just missed earnings and another is sinking this year. Why does Berkshire still hold on?
